scenarios.limitation: Repeating maize wears out the soil and does not spread the risk.

criteria.reason: Maize will need a lot of water, especially at flowering. In the NASA sample there was almost no rain on 3 of 7 days.
Planting maize again takes the same things from the soil and lets the same pests carry on.
It is the same crop: if it does badly, there is no other one to fall back on.

scenarios.summary: Beans are from another family: they help the soil and break the pest cycle of the previous crop.
scenarios.limitation: They need steady rain and cannot stand waterlogged soil.
scenarios.missingData: We do not know whether your soil waterlogs. With that detail, this option could move up or down.

criteria.reason: Beans will need less water than maize, but the rain has to be steady. In the NASA sample there was almost no rain on 3 of 7 days.
Beans are a legume: they help put nitrogen back into the soil.
It moves from a grass crop to a legume: two crops from different families spread the risk.

scenarios.summary: Sorghum copes better when the rain fails and leaves stubble that covers the soil.
scenarios.limitation: It is a relative of maize: the soil gets less rest than with beans.

criteria.reason: Sorghum can cope better with days without rain. In the NASA sample there was almost no rain on 3 of 7 days.
It is a change of crop, but sorghum and maize are relatives: the soil gets less rest.
It is a different crop, but from the same family.
